title: Equipment Running Hours Log
body: This sheet is the raw source under the A&U workbook and the daily production report — every ratio you see in a meeting was built from these meter readings. When Emp. No or fuel entries get skipped at shift-change, the fault signal that would have caught idling or a developing hydraulic problem never surfaces until it's a breakdown line item.
keyPoints: Diesel is fuel *issued*, not fuel *burned* — a unit can log large liters against zero hours (parked top-up) or low hours against high liters (idling or an early fault). Neither shows up in the A&U breakdown column. Check L/hr per unit, not just fleet totals.
Truck fleet carries ~60% of both hours and diesel on a normal day — 330-395 machine-hours, 25,000-29,000 L. If truck idling drops even 5%, that's roughly 1,300 L/day back.

The Emp. No column is the only place a named operator ties directly to a machine and shift. When an NCR or incident references a unit and time, this log tells you who was on it — pull it before you write the report, not after.

Zero-hour rows (Start = Stop) mean the unit didn't run — cross-check against the A&U breakdown-vs-standby split before assuming it was down. Roster-break Fridays and Eid-type holidays produce the same flat reading as a real fault.

Totals-row formulas can be wrong even when the sheet looks complete — one excavator diesel block was off by 1,940 L against its own row sum. Don't trust the summary cell blind; spot-check against the per-unit rows.
apply: If you're reviewing yesterday's shift handover, pull the running-hours tab alongside it — a unit burning fuel with flat hours is often the earliest tell on a fault before it hits the breakdown log.
